subject: Quant
description: Trigonometric ratios, special angles (0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°), Pythagorean identities, complementary angles, simple height-distance.

questions.stem: What is the value of sin 30° + cos 60°?
questions.explanation: STANDARD VALUES: sin 30° = 1/2, cos 60° = 1/2. So sin 30° + cos 60° = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1. KEY VALUES TABLE (memorize for SSC, NEET, JEE): sin: 0°=0, 30°=1/2, 45°=1/√2, 60°=√3/2, 90°=1. cos: 0°=1, 30°=√3/2, 45°=1/√2, 60°=1/2, 90°=0. tan: 0°=0, 30°=1/√3, 45°=1, 60°=√3, 90°=∞. COMPLEMENTARY-ANGLE FORMULAS: sin(90°−θ) = cos θ; cos(90°−θ) = sin θ; tan(90°−θ) = cot θ. So sin 30° = cos 60° (since 30° + 60° = 90°). MEMORIZATION TRICK: sin values from 0° to 90° = √0/2, √1/2, √2/2, √3/2, √4/2 = 0, 1/2, 1/√2, √3/2, 1. cos values are the reverse. PYTHAGOREAN IDENTITY: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 (always). PYQ FREQUENCY: standard angle values are a top SSC, JEE-Main, NEET 1-mark guarantee.

questions.stem: If sin θ = 3/5, then cos θ equals (assuming θ in first quadrant):
questions.explanation: Use the IDENTITY sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. So cos²θ = 1 − (3/5)² = 1 − 9/25 = 16/25. Therefore cos θ = ±4/5. In first quadrant (0° to 90°), cos θ > 0, so cos θ = 4/5. INTERPRETATION: in a right triangle, if sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse = 3/5, then opposite = 3, hypotenuse = 5; by Pythagoras adjacent = √(25−9) = √16 = 4. So cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse = 4/5. THE 3-4-5 TRIANGLE is the most famous Pythagorean triple — students should recognize it instantly. OTHER COMMON TRIPLES: (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), (7, 24, 25). KEY METHOD: when given one trig ratio, draw a right triangle, label the two known sides, find the third via Pythagoras, then read off any other ratio. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'find cos given sin' or vice-versa is a 1-mark guarantee in SSC CGL, JEE-Main. Quadrant sign awareness becomes critical in Class 11+ trig.

questions.stem: The value of tan 45° + cot 45° equals:
questions.explanation: tan 45° = 1, cot 45° = 1 (since cot = 1/tan). So tan 45° + cot 45° = 1 + 1 = 2. WHY tan 45° = 1? At 45°, sin = cos = 1/√2; so tan = sin/cos = 1. Same for cot. UNIQUE PROPERTY: 45° is the ONLY acute angle where tan θ = cot θ = 1 — useful for IDENTIFYING the angle in problems like 'tan A = cot A → A = 45°'. RECIPROCAL PAIRS: sin/csc, cos/sec, tan/cot. PRODUCTS: sin × csc = 1, cos × sec = 1, tan × cot = 1 (for any θ where defined). SAMPLE TRAP: 'tan 30° + cot 60°' — many students think they're equal (both = 1/√3); actually they ARE equal (cot 60° = 1/tan 60° = 1/√3 = tan 30°). PYQ ANGLE: standard-angle arithmetic appears 2-3× per JEE-Main, SSC CGL, NEET-style trig. KEY METHOD: memorize the value table, apply identities.

questions.stem: If tan θ = 1, then sin²θ + cos²θ + tan²θ equals:
questions.explanation: PYTHAGOREAN IDENTITY: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 — ALWAYS holds for any θ. tan θ = 1 → tan²θ = 1. So sin²θ + cos²θ + tan²θ = 1 + 1 = 2. ANGLE: tan θ = 1 → θ = 45° (in first quadrant). CHECK: sin 45° = cos 45° = 1/√2; sin² + cos² = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1 ✓. tan² = 1 ✓. Sum = 2 ✓. KEY IDENTITIES (memorize for SSC/JEE/NEET): (1) sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. (2) 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ. (3) 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ. APPLICATION — examiners build composite expressions to test which identity applies. SHORTCUT: anytime you see sin² + cos² in an expression, INSTANTLY replace with 1. PYQ FREQUENCY: identity-application Qs are 1-2 per JEE-Main, NEET, SSC CGL Tier 2 paper. EXAM TIP: don't compute sin/cos individually — apply identity first to simplify.

questions.stem: What is the value of sec²60° − tan²60°?
questions.explanation: PYTHAGOREAN IDENTITY: 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ → sec²θ − tan²θ = 1. This holds for ANY θ where sec θ is defined (θ ≠ 90°, 270°, etc.). So sec²60° − tan²60° = 1. VERIFY: sec 60° = 1/cos 60° = 1/(1/2) = 2 → sec²60° = 4. tan 60° = √3 → tan²60° = 3. Difference: 4 − 3 = 1 ✓. INSIGHT: examiners love this 'derive-and-verify' style — the IDENTITY gives the answer immediately, but plugging numbers also works (slower). PARALLEL IDENTITY: csc²θ − cot²θ = 1 (for θ ≠ 0°, 180°). MEMORIZATION TIP: there are 3 Pythagorean identities — one for each pair (sin/cos, sec/tan, csc/cot). Each comes from sin² + cos² = 1 by dividing by sin² or cos². PYQ FREQUENCY: identity-direct Qs are 1-2× per JEE-Main, SSC. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests fast-recall of the three identities; bonus for shortcut.

questions.stem: A pole of height 10 m casts a shadow of length 10√3 m. The angle of elevation of the sun is:
questions.explanation: tan(angle of elevation) = OPPOSITE / ADJACENT = pole-height / shadow-length = 10 / (10√3) = 1/√3. tan 30° = 1/√3, so angle = 30°. INTERPRETATION: when the sun is LOWER in the sky, shadows are LONGER — and the angle of elevation is SMALLER. SUN OVERHEAD (noon at equator): angle = 90°, shadow = 0 (theoretically). DAWN/DUSK: angle approaches 0°, shadow approaches infinity. PRACTICAL EXAMPLE: this is exactly how the great Egyptian astronomer ERATOSTHENES (~240 BCE) computed Earth's circumference — by comparing shadow lengths at Alexandria and Syene at solar noon. KEY METHOD for height-distance: (1) draw a right triangle. (2) identify opposite/adjacent. (3) use tan = opposite/adjacent. PYQ FREQUENCY: 1-2 height-distance Qs per SSC CGL Tier 2; JEE-Main rarely. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests trig-ratio recognition + practical-geometry application.

questions.explanation: Apply ANGLE-SUM IDENTITY: sin(A + B) = sin A · cos B + cos A · sin B. So sin 60° · cos 30° + cos 60° · sin 30° = sin(60° + 30°) = sin 90° = 1. DIRECT VERIFY: (√3/2)(√3/2) + (1/2)(1/2) = 3/4 + 1/4 = 1 ✓. ANGLE-SUM/DIFFERENCE IDENTITIES (memorize): (1) sin(A+B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B. (2) sin(A−B) = sin A cos B − cos A sin B. (3) cos(A+B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B. (4) cos(A−B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B. KEY FOR JEE-MAIN: lots of trig simplification problems hide angle-sum patterns — students who recognize the pattern solve in seconds. EXAM TRAP: many students compute each term separately (slow); spotting the identity is the elite shortcut. INSIGHT: this also gives derivation of double-angle: sin 2A = sin(A+A) = 2 sin A cos A. PYQ FREQUENCY: trigonometric simplification = 2-3 Qs per JEE-Main, NEET physics-side.
